name: Coca-Cola

header.one_liner: Volume is growing 5% and guidance went up; at 29x earnings the stock already prices that in.
header.thesis: Coca-Cola grew unit case volume 5% and organic revenue 7% in the third quarter, widened its comparable operating margin by a point and raised full-year guidance to at least 11% comparable EPS growth. The sale of its African bottling business will cut 2027 revenue by about 8% but raise margins. The franchise is excellent; the valuation leaves little to earn.

base.eps_label: FY2026E comparable EPS: guidance of at least 11% growth on 2025, in line with consensus
base.rev_label: FY2026E comparable net revenue ($B): 2025 $47.9B grown about 5% (organic growth plus currency, less divestitures)

rev_cagr.why: Organic revenue is guided to grow at least 5% in 2026, but the sale of the African bottling operations creates an 8% revenue headwind in 2027. The base case nets these to about 2% a year over three years: roughly -3% in 2027, then mid single digits.

margin_end.why: Net margin is about 29% today. Selling low-margin bottling operations lifts the group margin: the 8% revenue headwind costs only about 2% of EPS. The base case adds about three points over three years.
margin_end.source: Q3 2026 release (2027 considerations: revenue -8%, EPS -2% from divestitures)

share_chg.why: Buybacks run near $1B a year against a market value above $400B; most cash goes to the dividend.
share_chg.source: Statement of cash flows (trailing repurchases about $1.0B)

exit_pe.why: Today's multiple is about 29x 2026 comparable EPS, at the top of Coca-Cola's long-run range and far above PepsiCo and Keurig Dr Pepper. The base case assumes a de-rating toward 25x as growth returns to mid single digits.
exit_pe.source: Engine judgment; peer multiples from the Moat Monitor peer table

pillars.title: Volume is growing everywhere
pillars.claim: Unit case volume grew 5%, led by India, China, Mexico and Brazil; the company gained value share in nonalcoholic ready-to-drink beverages.

evidence.t: Unit case volume +5%; concentrate sales +7%; price/mix +1%

pillars.test: Does volume stay above 3% as pricing stays low?

pillars.title: Margins widened
pillars.claim: Comparable operating margin rose to 32.9% from 31.9% on revenue growth and currency, despite higher marketing.
pillars.test: Does margin hold when the currency tailwind fades?

pillars.title: Guidance raised
pillars.claim: Full-year comparable EPS growth raised to at least 11% from 9% to 10%, and free cash flow to at least $13.0B.

evidence.t: Organic revenue at least 5%; comparable currency neutral EPS ex divestitures at least 9%

pillars.test: Does 2027 guidance in February hold high single digits?

pillars.title: Refranchising shrinks revenue, lifts margins
pillars.claim: The pending sale of African bottling operations creates an 8% revenue headwind but only a 2% EPS headwind in 2027.

evidence.t: 2027 considerations: comparable net revenues about -8% and comparable EPS about -2% from acquisitions and divestitures

pillars.test: Does the deal close in Q4 as assumed?

variant.street: The market pays about 29x 2026 earnings, the top of Coca-Cola's range, for accelerating volume and raised guidance.
variant.ours: This is a very good year for a very good business, priced as if it lasts. Our base case grows EPS mid single digits and lets the multiple drift down, which earns less than the cost of equity over 12 months.
variant.could_be_wrong: If emerging-market volume keeps growing 5% and currency stays a tailwind, high-single-digit EPS growth supports today's multiple.
variant.would_change_mind: 2027 guidance above 8% comparable EPS growth, or the price falling toward 24x earnings.

moat.detail: Rated from the latest 10-K and 10-Q; see the moat window for the sources of advantage.

review.basis: Q3 2026 10-Q and release (quarter to 2 October 2026). Q4 and 2027 guidance come in February; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: A rare year of volume, margin and guidance all moving up. At 29x earnings, the stock already pays for it.
review.model: Coca-Cola makes concentrate and sells it to bottlers, which make, package and distribute the drinks. It earns high margins on concentrate and owns a few bottlers it is gradually selling.

how_it_earns.v: Syrups sold to independent bottlers. About 60% of revenue at very high margins.
Drinks sold directly, including fairlife and Costa. Lower margins.
Company-owned bottlers, being sold over time.
Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, fairlife, Powerade, Minute Maid, Costa.

mix.note: Reported segments. Operating margin is segment operating income over segment revenue, before corporate costs.

review.position: The largest nonalcoholic beverage company in the world, and gaining value share in ready-to-drink beverages.

moat.threat: Health trends and sugar taxes on soft drinks, and weight-loss drugs reducing consumption.

what_numbers_say.d: Led by India, China, Mexico and Brazil; organic revenue +7%.
Comparable EPS growth at least 11%; free cash flow at least $13.0B.
Divestitures cut 2027 revenue about 8% but EPS only about 2%.

balance.read: Solid: net debt about 1.2 times EBITDA, with most cash going to a dividend of $2.12 a share.
facts: African bottling sale expected to close in Q4 2026

flags.evidence: Concentrate sales grew 7% vs unit case volume 5%; the company attributes the gap to timing.
A 2-point currency tailwind to EPS in the quarter and about 3% for the year.
2027 revenue falls about 8% from divestitures; compare margins, not revenue.

forecast_basis.rev_cagr: Sourced: organic growth net of the divestiture headwind
forecast_basis.exit_pe: Judgment: drift down from the top of the historical range

base.story: Organic growth returns to mid single digits after this strong year; refranchising lifts margins; the multiple drifts toward 25x.

downside.story: Emerging-market volume slows and currency turns into a headwind; the multiple falls toward 21x.

upside.story: Volume keeps growing 5% and margins keep widening; high-single-digit EPS growth supports a high multiple.

risks.how: Growth this year comes mostly from India, China, Mexico and Brazil; a slowdown there takes volume first.
Sugar taxes and GLP-1 drugs could reduce how much people drink, especially in the US.
Currency added about 3% to EPS this year; a stronger dollar reverses it.
At 29x, a return to the middle of its historical range would cost 15% or more.
Coca-Cola has a long-running US tax dispute over transfer pricing; a final loss would require a large payment.

peer_read.why_premium: Coca-Cola has higher margins and faster volume growth than PepsiCo and Keurig Dr Pepper, and is more asset-light.
peer_read.why_not: At 27x next-year earnings it is far more expensive than PepsiCo (16x) and Keurig Dr Pepper (15x).
peer_read.peers_note: Monster trades higher still because it grows faster with no bottling assets.

questions: Is this year's volume growth repeatable?
How much of the multiple depends on falling interest rates?
Is a premium of about 70% to PepsiCo justified?

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Unit case volume grew 5% and organic revenue 7% in the third quarter. Full-year guidance was raised to at least 5% organic growth and 11% comparable EPS growth.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: The strongest brand portfolio in beverages and a bottling system that reaches almost everyone. Health trends and weight-loss drugs are the long-run threats.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Comparable operating margin rose a point to 32.9%. Selling the African bottlers cuts 2027 revenue about 8% but EPS only about 2%.

thesis_long: Coca-Cola is having one of its best years. Unit case volume grew 5% in the third quarter, led by India, China, Mexico and Brazil, organic revenue grew 7% and comparable operating margin widened by a point. Management raised full-year guidance to at least 11% comparable EPS growth and $13B of free cash flow.

The question is price. At about 29x this year's earnings the stock sits at the top of its historical range and about 70% above PepsiCo's multiple. Part of this year's growth came from currency (about 3 points of EPS) and concentrate shipments that ran ahead of consumer volume. 2027 will look smaller on paper as the African bottlers are sold, though margins rise.

Our base case grows EPS mid single digits and lets the multiple drift toward 25x, which earns less than the cost of equity over 12 months even for a low-risk stock. We would turn positive on 2027 guidance above 8% EPS growth or a price nearer 24x earnings.

upside_risks.how: Another year of 5% volume with price/mix would keep EPS growth high and support today's multiple.
Lower bond yields tend to lift defensive, dividend-paying stocks like Coca-Cola.
